status: exact non-overlapping uniform-sphere convolution for the 0-minus dipole-dipole kernel

domain.geometry: two uniformly polarized spheres of radii R_1 and R_2 with centre separation D>R_1+R_2
domain.polarization: constant species-weighted electron spin direction and density within each sphere
domain.exclusions: overlap, nonuniform domains, boundary-dependent polarization texture and magnetic backgrounds require a numerical apparatus model

formFactor.scalarConvolution: integral rho_1(x) rho_2(y) Y_m(|D+x-y|) d^3x d^3y=N_1 N_2 F(mR_1)F(mR_2)Y_m(D)
formFactor.tensorConvolution: global centre derivatives commute with both volume integrals, so the Hessian Yukawa kernel receives the identical multiplicative form factor

observable.transverseTorqueAmplitude: K_T=N_eff f_e^2 F(z1)F(z2) exp(-x)(x+1)/(4 pi D^3)
observable.radialEnergy: U_R=N_eff f_e^2 F(z1)F(z2) exp(-x)(x^2+2x+2)/(4 pi D^3)
observable.decision: uniform spherical finite size changes absolute reach but cancels exactly from the radial/transverse mass estimator

illustrativeGeometry.interpretation: at fixed total polarized counts, finite radius enhances the torque slightly because near-side pairs receive greater Yukawa weight; y_e reach improves by the square root of the torque form factor

decision: The finite-size blocker is analytically closed for uniform non-overlapping polarized spheres. A concrete experiment now needs only measured spin counts/textures, torque noise and a background model; arbitrary geometry can be handled by numerical convolution against this exact kernel.
